name: html-responsive-image-aspect-ratio-desktop
description: An authored with a RESPONSIVE crop (base `.hero-frame img{aspect-ratio:4/3;object-fit:cover}` plus a `@media (min-width:1024px){ .hero-frame img{aspect-ratio:5/6} }` desktop override) promotes the value that renders at the primary/desktop viewport. WordPress core/image carries a single aspectRatio, so the widest min-width breakpoint wins: the block gets 5/6 (portrait), not the 4/3 base (landscape), while scale stays cover. Three decoy overrides must all lose despite naming a WIDER min-width than the winner: a duplicate `@media (min-width:1024px)` declaring 3/4 that precedes the 5/6 rule (ties at one breakpoint go to the LAST rule, as the cascade decides them), a `@media not all and (min-width:1200px)` rule declaring 9/16 (negation inverts the feature test, so it applies BELOW 1200px), a `@media print and (min-width:1280px)` rule declaring 2/1 (a print crop is not the rendered screen crop), and a `@media (min-width:1300px) and (not (hover:hover))` rule declaring 7/8 (a negated feature the transformer cannot evaluate, and the one decoy the media-type check alone does not catch).

source_reference.notes: Derived from the portfolio-new hero (projects/portfolio-new/design/home.html) where .hero-frame img is 4/3 at base and 5/6 at min-width:1024px; the desktop viewport renders 5/6.

legacy_comparison.reason: Upstream primitive image behavior; no downstream legacy comparison.
